newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds dumped on dashed rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds dumped on dashed rate hopes.

text.p: *Australian debt markets were sold off heavily after today's stronger than expected local July retail trade data combined with a report suggesting the Fed is mulling a bigger rate hike.
*Hopes of an easing by the RBA seen put on hold.
Australian bonds and bills were sold off heavily as hopes of a local imminent rate cut were dashed, and the fear of a tightening by the Federal Reserve gathered momentum.

The U.S. air attack on Iraq pushed oil prices higher, but as Australia is a net exporter of oil, the Australian dollar was more likely to benefit rather than impact on the bonds from its inflationary implications, analysts said.
The 10-year bond yield spiked nearly 20 basis points to 8.30 percent, its highest level since end-July.
Meanwhile, the active December 90-day bill futures contract dropped around a 1/4 point, having priced in an easing to follow today's Reserve Bank board meeting.
The turning point for the market came when July retail trade came in at a much stronger than expected 2.4 percent growth compared with forecasts centring on a modest 0.4 percent rise.

"Markets viewed the figures negatively believing that strong consumer spending would delay any cuts to interest rates," said Hans Kunnen, State Bank NSW chief economist. "I do not buy that argument. Interest rates will need to fall if the government's growth and investment forecasts are to be achieved."
The retail growth came largely from the department store sector, which was seen reflecting recent price discounting by the retailers, analysts said.

Adding to the slide in domestic prices was an article in the Wall Street Journal saying Federal Reserve policy makers were leaning towards a bigger than expected 50 basis point hike in interest rates unless clear signs of slower growth emerges.

U.S. Treasury bond trading restarted in Tokyo today after Monday's U.S. Labor Day holiday and saw the key 30-year bond yield dip to 7.11 percent initially, before ratcheting to 7.15 percent on the WSJ report.

Yield spreads to other dollar bloc bonds reversed Monday's sharp narrowing as the local market went in retreat. The local yield curve was also flattened as a near term cut in interest rates was seen put on hold. Meanwhile, the U.S. market faces the U.S. NAPM index for August later today.
The September 10-year bond contract broke down through key levels at 91.830 and 91.770 as hedge fund selling triggered off stop-loss orders, leaving the close to 91.700 support at the close.
